dhp179:1: There is one whose victory cannot be turned to defeat,
dhp179:2: Unto victory over whom no one in the world can attain.
dhp179:3: The Buddha, unlimited in power, the trackless.
dhp179:4: By what track can you lead him?
dhp180:1: There is one in whom there is no Craving,
dhp180:2: With its snares and poisons, to lead him whithersoever.
dhp180:3: The Buddha, unlimited in power, the trackless.
dhp180:4: By what track can you lead him?
dhp181:1: They that are devoted to meditation, they that are steadfast,
dhp181:2: They that delight in the tranquillity of retirement from the world,
dhp181:3: They that are enlightened and mindful, they are beloved even of the gods.
dhp182:1: Difficult is it to obtain birth as a human being; difficult is the life of mortals;
dhp182:3: Difficult is the hearing of the Good Law; difficult is the rise of the Buddhas.
dhp183:1: The shunning of all evil, the doing of good,
dhp183:3: The cleansing of the heart: this is the Religion of the Buddhas.
dhp184:1: Patience, long-suffering, is the highest form of asceticism.
dhp184:2: Nibbāna the Buddhas declare to be the highest of all things.
dhp184:3: For one who strikes another is no true religious,
dhp184:4: Nor is he a monk who injures another.
dhp185:1: Not blaming, not harming, restraint under the Law,
dhp185:3: Moderation in food, a remote lodging,
dhp185:5: Dwelling on lofty thoughts, this is the Religion of the Buddhas.
dhp186:1: Not with a rain of coins can the lusts be satisfied;
dhp186:3: The wise man understands that the lusts afford but temporary satisfaction, and bring suffering in their train.
dhp187:1: Even in celestial pleasures the wise man takes no delight;
dhp187:3: The disciple of the Supremely Enlightened takes delight only in the destruction of Craving.
dhp188:1: To many a refuge men go, to mountains and to forests,
dhp188:3: To shrines and trees and groves, when terrified with fear.
dhp189:1: Such is no sure refuge, such is no final refuge;
dhp189:3: Not by resorting to such a refuge does a man obtain release from all suffering.
dhp190:1: Whoever seeks refuge in the Buddha, the Law, and the Order,
dhp190:3: Whoever, with clear understanding, beholds the Four Noble Truths,
dhp191:1: Suffering, the Origin of Suffering, the Escape from Suffering,
dhp191:3: And the Noble Eightfold Path of Escape from Suffering, –
dhp192:1: To this sure refuge, to this supreme refuge,
dhp192:3: By resorting to this refuge, he obtains release from all suffering.
dhp193:1: It is not easy to find a man of noble birth; it is not everywhere that such a man is born;
dhp193:3: Wherever is born a man that is steadfast, the family prospers wherein he is born.
dhp194:1: Pleasant is the rise of the Buddhas, pleasant is the preaching of the True Religion,
dhp194:3: Pleasant is peace and unity in the Order; the devotion of those who live in harmony is pleasant.
dhp195:1: He that renders honor to whom honor is due, whether they be the Buddhas or their disciples,
dhp195:3: Those that have overpassed the Hindrances, those that have crossed the Sea of Sorrow,
dhp196:1: He that renders honor to those that have found Nibbāna, to those that are without fear,
dhp196:4: His merit cannot be measured by anyone.
